Vote by mail or absentee

Can’t get to your polling place on Election Day? Here is how to vote by mail in Kansas, from the state’s own election office and its laws. Checked October 21, 2026.

Ask for your ballot by

Tuesday, October 27Passed

Your application for a ballot by mail must reach your county election office by Tuesday, October 27, 2026 (the Tuesday of the week before the election). (the law)

Send it back by

Tuesday, November 3Passed

Kansas law says a mailed ballot must reach your county election office by 7 p.m. on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3, 2026, and ballots handed in must arrive before the polls close. The Secretary of State's page adds that a court order now in force requires ballots postmarked by Election Day to be counted if they arrive by the last mail delivery on the Friday after the election (November 6, 2026). To be safe, get it there by 7 p.m. on Election Day. (official page)

The last day to ask for a ballot by mail has passed. You can still vote in person, early or on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3.You can still vote in person on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3. Early voting in person runs through Monday, November 2, 2026. When and where to vote early.

Kansas’s own page on voting by mail

At school away from home, in Kansas or in another state? What Kansas says about students is under Show more.

Who can vote by mail

No. Any registered Kansas voter can vote by mail (the state calls it "advance voting"); you do not need a reason. (official page)

How to ask for a ballot

  • By mail. Fill in and sign the state's Application for Advance Ballot (form AV1) and send it to your county election office. Give your Kansas driver's license or nondriver ID number, or include a copy of another accepted photo ID. You can ask for the ballot to be mailed to your registered address, a mailing address, or a temporary address where you are living. Open it (official page)
  • Email or fax. You can fax the signed application to your county election office, or email it; county email addresses are on the Secretary of State's county election officers list. Open it (official page)
  • In person. Vote an advance ballot in person at your county election office or a satellite site (see early voting below). Bring photo ID. (official page)

How to send it back

  • By mail. Mail it to your county election office. Kansas law says it must arrive by 7 p.m. on Election Day; see the note about the court order. (the law)
  • Drop box. Put it in any drop box in your own county. Drop boxes are locked when the polls close on Election Day. When we checked, the Secretary of State's page said its drop box list would be available soon; ask your county election office. (official page)
  • In person. Take it to your county election office, or to any polling place in your county, before the polls close on Election Day. Someone else may deliver it for you if you both sign a written statement that goes with the ballot; no one may deliver more than 10 other voters' ballots. (the law)

What the envelope needs

When you apply, give your Kansas driver's license or nondriver ID number, or send a copy of another accepted photo ID (such as a passport, a military ID, or a student ID from a Kansas college). The county checks the signature on your application against the one on file and will contact you if it does not match. Sign the ballot envelope too; if that signature does not match, the county must contact you. No witness or notary is needed. (the law)

Track your ballot

Track your ballot on Kansas’s own site (official page)

Vote early in person instead

Wednesday, October 14, 2026 to Monday, November 2, 2026.

Counties may start in-person advance voting as early as Wednesday, October 14, 2026 (20 days before the election); unless the county sets an earlier date, it starts Tuesday, October 27. It ends at 12 noon on Monday, November 2, 2026. Dates, hours and satellite sites vary by county; ask your county election office. (the law)

Students

At school in Kansas, away from home

The state's pages do not speak to students separately. Its general rule is that your residence for voting is the place you have adopted as home and mean to come back to whenever you are away. A student registered at home can ask for the ballot to be mailed to a temporary address, such as a school address. (the law)

At school in another state, with Kansas as home

The state's pages do not speak to students separately. Its general rule is that your residence for voting is the place you have adopted as home and mean to come back to when you are away. A Kansas voter living for a while in another state can ask for the ballot to be mailed to that temporary address. (the law)

Military and overseas

Active-duty military, their families and U.S. citizens living overseas apply with the Federal Post Card Application to the county they consider home; they do not need to be registered there first. An application sent before the primary also brings a ballot for the general election. Ballots go out starting 45 days before the election, and these voters may return them by mail, fax or email. The Federal Write-In Absentee Ballot is a backup if your ballot does not come in time. (official page)

Kansas in the Federal Voting Assistance Program’s guide

Good to know

  • Return deadline: a 2025 law ended Kansas's three-day grace period for mailed ballots starting in 2026, so the law says ballots must arrive by 7 p.m. on Election Day. The Secretary of State's advance voting page says a Douglas County court has ordered, statewide, that ballots postmarked by Election Day still be counted if they arrive by the last mail delivery on the Friday after the election, and that the Court of Appeals refused to pause that order for the general election. Court orders can change; mailing early or using a drop box avoids the question.
  • Ballots are mailed starting 20 days before the election (October 14, 2026).
  • Voters with a temporary illness or disability, or who are not proficient in reading English, can apply until the polls close on Election Day. People with a permanent disability or illness can ask for permanent advance voting status.
  • The Elections 101 booklet (used here for the signature rule) was written in 2022; its description of a three-day grace period is out of date.
  • The federal FVAP guide (source 8) lists Election Day, November 3, 2026, as the receipt deadline for military and overseas ballots.
